title: Testing Algerian Darija TTS: A Checklist for Scripts, Numbers, and Code-Switching
excerpt: Disclosure: I am sharing this guide from Natiq Studio. It is an English adaptation, with AI editing assistance, of our
content:
Disclosure: I am sharing this guide from Natiq Studio. It is an English adaptation, with AI editing assistance, of our Arabic guide to improving Darija scripts and pronunciation.

A successful text-to-speech request does not tell you whether the result says what the user intended. With Algerian Darija, the tricky cases often appear inside ordinary sentences: a French product term, a price, a place name, or a pause that lands in the wrong position.

Before changing the voice or regenerating a whole script, inspect the input. This checklist is a practical listening workflow for developers and creators integrating Darija speech into an application or content pipeline. It is not a benchmark or a promise of identical output on every generation.

1. Write the dialect you expect to hear

Selecting an Algerian voice does not automatically translate formal Arabic into everyday Darija. Start with the wording you actually want spoken.

Formal wording Darija wording to test
ماذا تنتظر؟ واش راك تستنى؟
سوف نرسل لك راح نبعتولك
هذا الشيء هاد الشي

These are contextual examples, not universal replacements. Read the script aloud before generating it. If a sentence feels awkward in ordinary conversation, simplify it before evaluating the synthetic voice.

Keep the meaning stable. A more conversational sentence should still communicate the same product information or instruction.

2. Treat punctuation as a hypothesis

Break a long sentence into clear ideas. A script that combines the product, delivery terms, price, and guarantee in one breath is difficult to judge and can be difficult to follow.

Listen to the result after adding a comma or splitting a sentence. Do not assume that a comma creates a fixed half-second pause, or that extra exclamation marks reliably produce the intended emotion. Punctuation can influence the reading, but the actual output needs checking.

For a product workflow, confirm that edits preserve the real offer. Improving delivery should never introduce an unsupported refund promise, delivery area, or availability claim.

3. Isolate mixed French terms and names

When a word is mispronounced, test it in a short sentence before rerunning the entire script. Common terms may benefit from an Arabic phonetic spelling, such as ليفريزون or بروموسيون.

Compare that spelling with the version you were already using, while keeping the voice and surrounding text unchanged. Different voices and contexts may produce different results; one successful spelling does not establish a rule for every French word.

Apply the same process to brand and place names. For example, test زيتا for Zeta or the Arabic spelling باب الزوار for Bab Ezzouar. Check that the new spelling still identifies the intended name.

4. Check numbers for meaning, not just fluency

Prices, phone numbers, dates, and quantities have different reading requirements. A phone number may need digits read individually, while a price should communicate a monetary amount clearly.

Write the amount as you intend it to be spoken, then listen to it separately. If the script uses a colloquial expression in centimes, verify that it matches the amount displayed in Algerian dinars.

A natural-sounding voice can still communicate the wrong price. Compare the audio with the visible interface, product card, or caption before releasing it.

5. Change one variable at a time

To compare two voices, generate the same text with each voice. To compare two spellings, keep the voice fixed and change only the spelling under investigation.

Listen for:

  • Whether the word is understandable.
  • Whether the pause supports the sentence's meaning.
  • Whether the voice and pace suit the intended context.
  • Whether numbers and names retain their intended meaning.

Limited diacritics can be tested when a word is ambiguous. There is no need to add full diacritics to every dialect word without checking how the engine responds.

This process makes comparisons easier to interpret. Changing the voice, punctuation, spelling, and sentence structure together makes it harder to identify which edit helped.

6. Review the final playback context

A clean audio sample is only part of the review. Put it alongside the actual video, captions, or interface and check that the relevant information is heard when it appears on screen.

If there is background music, make sure it does not cover the speech. Correct pronunciation first; music should not be used to hide a word that is wrong. Also listen on an ordinary phone rather than relying only on good headphones.

Trying the workflow with Natiq Studio

In Natiq Studio, enter Darija text in Arabic script, select a voice, and test a short passage before generating the full script. The hosted service provides WAV downloads; converting that file to MP3 is a separate step in an audio editor.

The hosted product uses selectable voices and does not support uploading someone else's recording to clone their voice. Keep that distinction clear when describing a speech workflow to users.

For the original examples and script-writing background, see our Darija pronunciation guide.

Before shipping

  • Is the text written in the dialect the user should hear?
  • Are French terms and proper names understandable?
  • Does the spoken price match the displayed amount?
  • Do pauses support the message?
  • Is speech clear in the final playback context?

Start with one small change, listen, and decide what to test next. The useful result is a script that communicates accurately in its intended setting, not simply a request that completed successfully.

title: Moving Data Between Shopify Stores Is More Complicated Than It Should Be
excerpt: One thing that can be frustrating when running a Shopify store is moving data from one store to another.
content:
One thing that can be frustrating when running a Shopify store is moving data from one store to another.

At first, it might seem like a simple process. You export your data from the original store and import it into the new one. However, once you start dealing with different types of content, you may realize that not everything can be transferred as easily as you expected.

Products, customers, and orders are one part of the process, but what about other store content?

Depending on the type of data involved, you may also need to deal with blogs and articles, pages, menus, metafields, custom data, theme settings, files, and other store-specific configurations.

Some information can be exported and imported using Shopify's built-in features, while other content may require additional steps or manual work. In some cases, the data might transfer, but its relationships, formatting, or functionality may not remain exactly the same.

This creates several challenges for store owners:

Time-consuming manual work: Recreating pages, content, or settings one by one can take hours or even days.

Incomplete transfers: Not all types of store data follow the same export and import process.

Formatting issues: Content may appear differently after being moved to another store.

Missing relationships: Certain references, custom fields, or connected data may need to be checked and updated.

Risk of mistakes: When handling a large amount of data manually, it is easy to overlook something important.

The problem becomes even more noticeable when a business is redesigning its store, separating a business into multiple stores, changing its store structure, or migrating to a new setup.

Of course, not every type of data should necessarily be transferred automatically. Some information depends on the theme, installed apps, store configuration, or specific business requirements. That is understandable.

Still, it would be helpful to have clearer options for identifying which data can be transferred directly, which requires extra steps, and which needs to be recreated manually.

A more flexible migration process could save store owners a lot of time and reduce the risk of losing important content during a move.

I'm curious about other Shopify store owners' experiences:

Have you ever needed to move content from one Shopify store to another?

Which types of data were the most difficult to transfer?

Did you have to recreate anything manually that you expected to be transferable?

What improvements would make the process easier?

It would be interesting to hear how others have handled this, especially those who have migrated larger stores or worked with content beyond products and orders.

title: Kiểm tra AI crawler có đọc được site không: robots.txt, HTML ban đầu và log server
excerpt: Tuần trước một người quen nhờ mình xem vì sao ChatGPT trả lời về công ty anh ấy toàn thông tin cũ. Nội dung không sai, schema cũng có. Kiểm tra một lúc mới ra nguyên nhân rất "dev": robots.txt đang
content:
Tuần trước một người quen nhờ mình xem vì sao ChatGPT trả lời về công ty anh ấy toàn thông tin cũ. Nội dung không sai, schema cũng có. Kiểm tra một lúc mới ra nguyên nhân rất "dev": robots.txt đang chặn một bot tìm kiếm của AI, còn trang dịch vụ thì phần mô tả chỉ hiện ra sau khi JavaScript chạy xong.

Bài này ghi lại cách mình kiểm tra theo ba lớp: robots.txt, HTML ban đầu và log server. Toàn bộ chỉ cần terminal, curl, grep và quyền đọc access log. Mình không bàn chuyện nội dung hay thực thể ở đây, chỉ xem bot có vào được và đọc được hay không.

Các user-agent nên biết

Không có danh sách nào đầy đủ mãi, nhưng đây là những cái mình hay gặp nhất:

  • GPTBot (OpenAI): thu thập nội dung có thể dùng để huấn luyện mô hình. Chặn GPTBot nghĩa là bạn không muốn nội dung bị dùng cho việc đó.
  • OAI-SearchBot (OpenAI): dùng cho tính năng tìm kiếm của ChatGPT. Theo tài liệu của OpenAI, site chặn bot này sẽ không xuất hiện trong câu trả lời tìm kiếm của ChatGPT (vẫn có thể hiện dạng link điều hướng).
  • ChatGPT-User (OpenAI): truy cập khi người dùng yêu cầu ChatGPT mở một trang. OpenAI ghi rõ đây là hành động do người dùng khởi tạo nên robots.txt có thể không áp dụng.
  • ClaudeBot (Anthropic) và PerplexityBot (Perplexity): crawler của hai nền tảng này.
  • Google-Extended: chỉ là một token trong robots.txt, không có user-agent riêng nên bạn sẽ không thấy nó trong log. Google dùng nó để bạn chọn có cho nội dung phục vụ Gemini hay không; nó không ảnh hưởng tới việc trang có lên Google Search. AI Overviews vẫn đi theo Googlebot và index thông thường.

Điểm quan trọng: ba bot của OpenAI là ba thiết lập độc lập. Bạn hoàn toàn có thể mở OAI-SearchBot để được tìm thấy trong ChatGPT search mà vẫn chặn GPTBot.

Lớp 1: đọc robots.txt cho đúng

Đầu tiên lấy file về:

curl -s https://example.com/robots.txt

Chỗ nhiều người đọc nhầm: một crawler chỉ theo nhóm user-agent khớp cụ thể nhất với nó. Nếu file có nhóm User-agent: GPTBot thì GPTBot bỏ qua hoàn toàn nhóm User-agent: *, kể cả các dòng Disallow bạn tưởng là áp dụng cho mọi bot. Ví dụ:

User-agent: *
Disallow: /admin/

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

Ở đây GPTBot bị chặn toàn site, còn OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot rơi vào nhóm * nên chỉ bị chặn /admin/. Nếu bạn muốn cho bot tìm kiếm vào nhưng chặn bot huấn luyện, viết rõ từng nhóm:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /

Mình hay lọc nhanh các dòng liên quan bằng:

curl -s https://example.com/robots.txt \
  | grep -inE -A3 'user-agent: *(\*|gptbot|oai-searchbot|chatgpt-user|claudebot|perplexitybot|google-extended)'

Hai lỗi mình gặp nhiều nhất: plugin bảo mật hoặc CDN tự thêm nhóm chặn "AI bots" mà chủ site không biết, và robots.txt bị trả về 403 hoặc trang HTML lỗi thay vì file text. Kiểm tra luôn status và content-type:

curl -sI https://example.com/robots.txt | grep -iE '^(HTTP|content-type)'

OpenAI cũng lưu ý thay đổi robots.txt có thể mất khoảng 24 giờ để hệ thống tìm kiếm của họ cập nhật, nên đừng sửa xong rồi thử ngay.

Lớp 2: gọi trang bằng user-agent của bot và xem HTML ban đầu

robots.txt cho phép không có nghĩa là server cho phép. WAF, Cloudflare hay rule chống bot có thể trả 403, 429 hoặc trang challenge cho đúng mấy user-agent này. Mình giả lập bằng curl:

URL="https://example.com/dich-vu/abc"

for UA in \
  "Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot" \
  "Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; ChatGPT-User/1.0; +https://openai.com/bot" \
  "OAI-SearchBot/1.4" \
  "ClaudeBot/1.0" \
  "PerplexityBot/1.0"
do
  printf '%-20s ' "$(echo "$UA" | grep -oE '(GPTBot|ChatGPT-User|OAI-SearchBot|ClaudeBot|PerplexityBot)')"
  curl -s -o /dev/null -A "$UA" -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' "$URL"
done

Chuỗi user-agent đầy đủ có số phiên bản thay đổi theo thời gian; với việc kiểm tra rule chặn theo tên thì chỉ cần chứa đúng tên bot là đủ. Kết quả cần nhìn: mọi dòng nên là 200 và kích thước gần bằng nhau. Một dòng 403, hoặc 200 nhưng chỉ vài KB trong khi trình duyệt nhận cả trăm KB, thường là trang challenge.

Lưu ý: cách này chỉ kiểm tra được rule chặn theo user-agent. Nếu firewall chặn theo IP hoặc ASN thì curl từ máy bạn vẫn qua, còn bot thật thì không. Vì vậy cần lớp 3.

Nội dung có nằm trong HTML ban đầu không

Nhiều bot AI đọc HTML trả về chứ không chạy JavaScript như trình duyệt. Nếu site là SPA render phía client, bot có thể chỉ thấy một <div id="root"></div> trống.

Cách kiểm tra đơn giản: chọn một câu quan trọng (tên dịch vụ, giá, địa chỉ) và grep trong HTML thô:

curl -s -A "GPTBot/1.4" "$URL" | grep -c "Dịch vụ thiết kế website"

Ra 0 thì có hai khả năng: nội dung do JS tạo ra, hoặc chuỗi bị encode thành HTML entity. Để chắc, mình bỏ thẻ và xem phần text thô:

curl -s -A "GPTBot/1.4" "$URL" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,re,html; t=sys.stdin.read(); t=re.sub(r'<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>','',t,flags=re.S); t=html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>','\n',t)); print('\n'.join(l.strip() for l in t.splitlines() if l.strip()))" \
  | head -50

Nếu 50 dòng đầu chỉ có menu, footer và "Loading...", đó là dấu hiệu nội dung chính không nằm trong HTML ban đầu. Hướng sửa thường là SSR, SSG hoặc prerender cho các trang quan trọng; tùy framework mà cách làm khác nhau.

Cũng nên kiểm tra thêm <title>, meta description và thẻ <meta name="robots"> trong HTML thô, vì có site gắn noindex bằng JS rồi quên gỡ:

curl -s "$URL" | grep -oiE '<(title|meta name="(description|robots)")[^>]*>[^<]*'

Lớp 3: đọc access log

Đây là nơi trả lời câu hỏi "bot có thực sự ghé không". Với log nginx hoặc Apache dạng combined:

# Đếm lượt truy cập theo từng bot (gồm cả log đã nén)
zgrep -hoiE 'GPTBot|OAI-SearchBot|ChatGPT-User|ClaudeBot|PerplexityBot' /var/log/nginx/access.log* \
  | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Xem bot gặp status nào, ở URL nào
grep -iE 'GPTBot|OAI-SearchBot|ClaudeBot|PerplexityBot' /var/log/nginx/access.log \
  | awk '{print $9, $7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30

Nếu thấy nhiều 403 hoặc 429, quay lại xem rule WAF hoặc rate limit. Nếu hoàn toàn không có dòng nào sau vài tuần, có thể bot chưa biết tới site, hoặc bị chặn từ tầng CDN trước khi request tới server; khi đó cần xem log hoặc dashboard của CDN.

User-agent thì ai cũng giả được. OpenAI công bố dải IP cho từng bot ở các file JSON như https://openai.com/gptbot.json, searchbot.json, chatgpt-user.json. Mình kiểm tra một IP trong log như sau:

IP="20.171.206.10"
curl -s https://openai.com/gptbot.json \
  | jq -r '.prefixes[] | .ipv4Prefix // .ipv6Prefix' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,ipaddress; ip=ipaddress.ip_address('$IP'); print(any(ip in ipaddress.ip_network(l.strip()) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()))"

Ra True thì đúng là bot của OpenAI. Với các bot khác, xem trang tài liệu crawler của từng bên để lấy cách xác minh tương ứng.

Checklist ngắn

  1. robots.txt trả 200, text/plain, không có nhóm chặn bot mà bạn không chủ động thêm.
  2. Mỗi bot bạn muốn cho vào được xử lý đúng nhóm user-agent của nó, không trông vào nhóm *.
  3. curl với từng user-agent đều ra 200 và kích thước tương đương trình duyệt.
  4. Câu quan trọng nhất của trang có trong HTML thô, không cần JS.
  5. Không có noindex ngoài ý muốn trong HTML ban đầu.
  6. Log có lượt truy cập từ bot, status chủ yếu là 200, IP khớp dải được công bố.
  7. Trang đã được Google index, vì AI Overviews chỉ lấy nguồn từ trang đủ điều kiện hiển thị trên Google Search.

Ba lớp này chỉ trả lời câu hỏi bot có đọc được site hay không. Đọc được rồi mà AI vẫn tả sai công ty thì vấn đề nằm ở nội dung và nguồn bên ngoài; phần đó mình đã viết riêng trong checklist 30 phút tìm lý do ChatGPT mô tả sai doanh nghiệp.

Nếu bạn không có quyền đọc log hay không muốn tự mò rule CDN, Mạnh Digital có dịch vụ tối ưu cho AI search, trong đó phần kỹ thuật gồm đưa nội dung quan trọng vào HTML ban đầu và cấu hình robots.txt cho các bot AI. Còn nếu tự làm, chạy hết checklist trên một lần là đã loại được phần lớn lỗi mình hay gặp.

title: Why I Built API.market After PipFeed
excerpt:
I am Shashank Agarwal, the creator of API.market and founder and CEO of Noveum AI. Before either company, I built a personalized reading app called PipFeed.

The app did not become the busin
content:
I am Shashank Agarwal, the creator of API.market and founder and CEO of Noveum AI. Before either company, I built a personalized reading app called PipFeed.

The app did not become the business I hoped it would. But a service inside it turned out to be useful on its own.

That experience changed how I think about building products: a product can struggle while one of its components solves a problem people will pay to remove.

The useful component inside a difficult business

PipFeed needed to extract article content from web pages so the reading experience could work. That meant building infrastructure to turn messy pages into usable content.

After closing the mobile app, I continued with the parsing API. I described that pivot publicly in a November 2023 update.

There are two separate decisions in a pivot like this.

First, does the component have value beyond the original product? A parsing service might help a reading app, a research workflow, or a content-processing pipeline.

Second, can someone else use it without inheriting all the complexity of your application? That requires a clear interface, understandable inputs and outputs, documentation, and a way to pay.

The second question is where a useful internal service becomes an actual product.

An API needs a commercial workflow

Putting an endpoint on the internet is only part of selling an API.

A developer needs to discover it, decide whether it fits, understand the price, make an authenticated request, and inspect the result. A provider needs to publish the service, meter usage, manage access, and support customers.

The experience selling the PipFeed API pushed me toward these problems. I explain that origin in API.market's early About Us documentation.

I built API.market around the journey on both sides of the transaction. It is a marketplace for APIs and AI models, with discovery, access, provider publishing, metering, and billing.

For someone building an API product, I would start by writing down the first five minutes of a customer's experience:

  1. What problem brought them to the page?
  2. Can they see the required inputs and a realistic output?
  3. Can they understand how the service charges for usage?
  4. Can they make a request and inspect a failure?
  5. Do they know what to do next if the service fits?

A marketplace does not remove the need for a good API. It has to make the API easier to evaluate and use.

What AI agents change

The customer operating an API is increasingly an AI agent acting on a person's behalf.

That creates an additional interface problem. A human can read a pricing page, compare documentation, and reason about an error. An agent needs discoverable operations, usable schemas, authentication, and boundaries around paid actions.

API.market's MCP gateway is one way we connect compatible AI clients to the marketplace. The gateway gives the client a path to discover services and call operations.

Connecting a tool does not settle every decision. The underlying API still has its own behavior, limits, and pricing. An agent's ability to make a call should be considered separately from permission to incur a charge or take a consequential action.

An example: a workflow that extracts ten articles should establish which parser to use, what the calls cost, what counts as a valid extraction, and what to do when a page cannot be parsed. “The tool returned something” is a weak acceptance criterion.

Why this connects to Noveum

I worked on production machine learning at AWS and Amazon, including the original SageMaker launch team and later personalization work at Prime Video. That background made the operational side of AI familiar: a working model is one part of a working system.

At Noveum, the focus is production AI agents. Teams need to capture what happened, evaluate whether the behavior met the task's requirements, investigate failures, and review evidence for a change.

The connection to API.market is practical. One business helps developers and agents access tools. The other helps teams examine what agents actually do.

Consider an agent that extracts an article and summarizes it. A successful HTTP response does not establish that the extraction included the relevant section, that the summary is grounded, or that the workflow stayed within its budget. Those are different checks.

That distinction is useful even if you never use either product. Define the intended outcome before choosing the tools, and inspect the evidence before calling the workflow successful.

The lesson I keep coming back to

The path from PipFeed to API.market was not a straight line. It involved recognizing that the app and the service inside it had different customers and different business possibilities.

For builders, the useful question is concrete: which piece of your product already removes a recurring problem for someone else?

Then do the less visible work: make it understandable, accessible, measurable, and supportable.

I write about that work, production AI, and developer products on LinkedIn.

Disclosure: I founded Noveum AI and created API.market. The product examples above describe my own companies. They are not independent product reviews.

title: Architecting Production Technical SEO: Real-Time Core Web Vitals (INP, LCP, CLS) and HTTP Security Hardening
excerpt: In modern web engineering, technical SEO is no longer about keyword stuffing or static XML sitemaps. Search engine bots (such as Googlebot and Bingbot) execute headless Chromium rendering pipelines
content:
In modern web engineering, technical SEO is no longer about keyword stuffing or static XML sitemaps. Search engine bots (such as Googlebot and Bingbot) execute headless Chromium rendering pipelines that evaluate client-side performance budgets, Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), and cryptographic HTTP security headers directly during crawling and indexing.

A web application that scores high in synthetic lab tests (e.g., local Lighthouse runs with unthrottled CPU) frequently fails real-world field evaluations across mobile networks. Below is an architectural overview of how to build automated auditing pipelines to measure, debug, and harden production web platforms.

1. Demystifying Interaction to Next Paint (INP) in Heavy DOM Trees

When Google deprecated First Input Delay (FID) in favor of INP (Interaction to Next Paint), the metric shifted from measuring initial event latency to measuring the longest interaction duration throughout the entire lifecycle of a user session.

INP measures three distinct phases:

  1. Input Delay: Time between user input (click, tap, keypress) and when the event handler begins execution.
  2. Processing Time: Execution duration of all synchronous JavaScript callbacks attached to the event.
  3. Presentation Delay: Time needed by the browser compositor and render tree to repaint the viewport.

Common Bottlenecks and Architectural Remedies:

  • Long Tasks on Main Thread: Break CPU-bound loops using scheduler.yield() or requestIdleCallback().
  • Forced Synchronous Layout (Reflows): Never query layout properties (offsetHeight, getBoundingClientRect()) immediately after mutating DOM styles.
  • Hydration Freezes in SSR Frameworks: Utilize selective hydration, server components, and islands architecture so users can interact with elements before background JavaScript completes.

In our production audits at SEOAudit, we consistently observe that over 68% of e-commerce and SaaS sites fail INP due to third-party tracking pixels attached to non-passive touch listeners.

2. Optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) Under Real-World Latency

LCP represents the moment when the largest visible element (typically an hero banner, H1 typography element, or featured picture) is painted on screen.

Key optimization checklist:

<!-- 1. Eliminate render-blocking CSS by inlining critical viewport styles -->
<link rel="preload" fetchpriority="high" as="image" href="/assets/hero-banner.webp" type="image/webp">

<!-- 2. Self-host critical fonts and specify font-display: swap -->
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter-variable.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>

Practical case study: On technical infrastructure portals such as SunEco (solar microgrid sizing) and Svitlo-Lux (condominium backup power systems), replacing external web fonts with self-hosted subset variable fonts combined with Brotli compression dropped LCP from 2.9s down to 0.85s on 4G mobile connections.

3. Cryptographic Security Headers in Technical Audits

Modern search engines penalize insecure sites and down-rank pages exhibiting mixed content or missing transport security. An exhaustive technical audit must inspect the following HTTP headers:

Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)

Enforces HTTPS across the root domain and all subdomains:

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload

Content-Security-Policy (CSP)

Prevents cross-site scripting (XSS) and unauthorized data injection:

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://apis.google.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://api.seoaudit.com.ua;

Essential Hardening Headers:

  • X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  • X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (or frame-ancestors self in CSP)
  • Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
  • Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

4. Canonicalization and Crawler Bot Rendering

When indexing dynamic single-page applications, search crawlers allocate a finite "render budget". If your application requires more than 5 seconds of client-side execution to render meta tags, rel="canonical", or OpenGraph properties, crawlers may index blank shells.

  • Dynamic Edge Rendering: Serve lightweight pre-rendered HTML to verified bot user-agents (Googlebot, Bingbot, YandexBot) using Cloudflare Workers or Vercel Edge Middleware.
  • Strict Canonical Trailing Slash Policies: Prevent duplicate content penalties by enforcing consistent redirect policies (301 Permanent Redirects) for trailing slashes, www vs non-www, and uppercase paths.

5. Automation and Continuous Auditing

To maintain optimal technical health, teams should incorporate automated crawling into their CI/CD deployment pipelines. You can utilize open-source scanners or specialized platforms like SEOAudit.com.ua to evaluate page speed, Core Web Vitals, broken canonical chains, and HTTP header security before shipping code to production.

What performance budgets or CI/CD audit tools are you running in your stack? Share your approach in the comments below!

title: Letting Claude maintain WordPress sites without giving it SSH access
excerpt: I look after WordPress sites for a living, and lately I've wanted Claude to take over the boring parts: find where a piece of text lives in a theme, fix it, check which plugins need updates, write
content:
I look after WordPress sites for a living, and lately I've wanted Claude to take over the boring parts: find where a piece of text lives in a theme, fix it, check which plugins need updates, write the monthly care report for the client.

The two obvious ways to do that both felt wrong:

  • Give the AI an SSH key. It sees everything, including wp-config.php and the database password, and one bad instruction can wipe a client's site.
  • Copy and paste files into a chat. Safe, but slow, and the AI never sees the whole theme.

So I built something in between: PressBridge, a self-hosted MCP server that sits between Claude and the WordPress site. Claude gets useful tools; the server decides what those tools are allowed to do.

The server enforces the rules, not the prompt

A prompt like "never read wp-config.php" is a suggestion. A file that is invisible to the tool is a guarantee. That was the main design rule: every limit is checked by PressBridge before anything runs, so text hidden in a plugin readme or a web page can't talk Claude past it.

In the free edition, Claude can:

  • read, list and search theme and plugin files
  • run read-only WP-CLI commands: versions, plugin and theme lists, core checksums, cron, users
  • call site_overview to get the WordPress version and pending updates in one call

And it can't:

  • see wp-config.php, .env, SQL dumps, keys or .git, at any folder depth
  • reach anything outside the site folder, symlink tricks included
  • open a shell or run arbitrary commands

It connects over SSH, so nothing is exposed to the internet.

A real session

Here's a 70-second recording of a real session on a test site: health overview, creating and editing a file with an automatic backup, a one-call undo, a safe delete and the audit log.

Try it

The free edition is MIT-licensed on GitHub, for one site, read-only: https://github.com/pressbridgesupport/pressbridge

Install takes about five minutes on any Linux server where you have SSH: a Python venv, WP-CLI, and a small YAML file listing your site. Then add it to Claude Code or Claude Desktop and ask: "Give me a health overview of mysite."

If you want Claude to fix things too

I also sell a paid edition, which is how I'm hoping to keep working on this. It adds edits with automatic backups and one-call undo, a PHP syntax check before saving, allow-listed plugin, theme and core updates, unlimited sites, a Docker HTTPS server and a full audit log. There's also a monthly plan with a nightly security check that alerts you to new admin accounts, PHP files in uploads and changed core files. Details: https://pressbridgesupport.github.io/pressbridge

One honest limit: file backups don't cover database changes such as plugin updates, so keep your normal database backups running.

Feedback welcome

I'd really like to hear from people who manage WordPress sites: what would you want blocked, or allowed, before you'd let an AI assistant anywhere near a client site?

Dynadot Renewals in 2026: The $10.88 .com Nobody Talks About

Everyone talks about GoDaddy and Namecheap. Almost nobody talks about Dynadot — and that's a shame, because its renewal pricing is one of the most honest in the industry.

The flat $10.88 renewal

Dynadot charges $10.88/year to renew a .com — and unlike most big registrars, the price doesn't jump between your first year and your renewal. What you see is what you keep paying. Compare that to the industry norm: GoDaddy renews around $22.99, Namecheap around $18.48, Hostinger around $19.99.

That's roughly $10+ saved every year, per domain, just by being at the right registrar.

Why Dynadot stays cheap

Dynadot's business model is simple: thin margins, no loss-leader intro pricing, no upsell maze at checkout. Their price sits just above wholesale cost (Verisign's wholesale .com price is $10.26 plus the $0.18 ICANN fee, and it's rising to $10.97 on 1 November 2026) — so there's no artificial discount waiting to expire on you.

I wrote a full breakdown of Dynadot's renewal pricing, transfer process, and where it beats the competition here: Dynadot Domain Renewal Review 2026: Is the $10.88 .com Renewal Worth It?

Do the 5-year math

Before you renew anywhere, multiply the renewal price by 5 and compare it to the alternatives. Here's the cheapest end of the market right now:

  • Dynadot: 5 × $10.88 = $54.40
  • Spaceship: 5 × $10.18 = $50.90
  • Porkbun: 5 × $11.08 = $55.40
  • Cloudflare: 5 × $10.44 = $52.20 (at-cost pricing, no markup)

Full side-by-side comparison with every major registrar: Cheapest .com Renewal Prices in 2026

A quick renewal audit (do this today)

  1. Log in to your registrar and check the renewal price, not the registration price.
  2. Check the expiry date — set a reminder 60 days before.
  3. If your renewal is $18+ and you're not locked in, get your auth/EPP code and transfer to a cheaper registrar. Transfers usually include a free extra year.
  4. Turn auto-renew ON once you're at a registrar with a fair price.

You can compare all major registrars' renewal prices side by side here: RenewPings Compare

The cheapest domain is the one you never overpay to renew.

title: Serverless & AI in brief: week 43/2026
excerpt: Serverless & AI in brief is my new weekly review: every Monday I sort through the previous week’s news from AWS, serverless, AI tools and TypeScript/Node.js and explain what it means for you as
content:
Serverless & AI in brief is my new weekly review: every Monday I sort through the previous week’s news from AWS, serverless, AI tools and TypeScript/Node.js and explain what it means for you as a developer or team lead. For each item I read the primary source, meaning release notes, security bulletins and changelogs, not just the headlines.

Calendar week 43 (October 19 to 25, 2026) was a week for cleaning up. A certificate incident hit several ecosystems at once, Node.js shipped important security updates, and the Claude API got a new version with breaking changes. On top of that, a few new features will save you work in everyday life.

What you will learn in this article

  • Which AWS deadlines the eMudhra incident triggers from October 28
  • Which Node.js versions you should run now and why
  • What to check before upgrading to the new Claude SDKs
  • Which updates to GitHub, CloudFormation and TypeScript are worth a look

Security updates that cannot wait

Three of the seven items are about security. That is no coincidence, because they are connected: the certificate incident triggered updates in browsers, runtimes and at AWS.

eMudhra certificates: AWS sets deadlines from October 28

On October 17, Mozilla received a report that the private keys of eight intermediate certificates from the certificate authority eMudhra had been compromised. An intermediate CA issues website certificates on behalf of a root CA. With those keys, someone could create valid-looking certificates for other people’s domains. Firefox blocked the certificates the same evening, and Mozilla also removed the issuing root from its NSS certificate store. AWS followed on October 24 with Security Bulletin 2026-150-AWS: three roots are being removed from the AWS trust stores. CloudFront is scheduled to stop trusting them for origin connections from October 28, and Application Load Balancers with OIDC or JWT authentication follow from October 29 to 31. Updates are already available for Amazon Corretto, the ca-certificates package in Amazon Linux and botocore (version 1.43.117 and later).

What this means for you: if a CloudFront distribution sits in front of an origin with its own certificate that was not issued through ACM, check the certificate chain before Wednesday. The same applies to identity providers behind an ALB. My article eMudhra certificates: check Java, Node, Python and Go shows how to check the chain in each language.

Node.js 26.12.1, 24.22.1 and 22.23.4 close an RCE flaw

On October 21, the Node.js project released security updates for all three supported release lines. They fix ten CVEs, four of them rated “High”. The most serious is CVE-2026-111497: with manipulated input, the bundled Brotli decoder writes past the end of an internal buffer. If you decompress Brotli data from untrusted sources with node:zlib, the worst case is remote code execution. Security researchers have since demonstrated an exploit called “Node2Shell”. The releases also ship updated CA certificates because of the eMudhra incident.

I would prioritize this update because it solves two problems at once. AWS updates the managed Lambda runtimes itself, but container images, CI runners, pinned runtime versions and local environments are your job. In Node2Shell: close CVE-2026-111497 now I describe the attack paths and how to check your Lambda functions.

GitHub Package Firewall checks npm packages before install

Since October 20, GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can try the new Package Firewall as a public preview. The firewall stands between your machines, CI runners or coding agents and the package registry and checks every download against rules. These include a configurable waiting period for new versions (cooldown), a lookup in the GitHub Advisory Database to see whether malware has been reported for a package, and detection of downgraded attestations. For now only npm is supported. The preview is free; later, billing will be usage-based.

In my view, the cooldown is the biggest lever. Many supply chain attacks in recent months relied on a compromised version landing on thousands of machines within a few hours. If you let new versions sit for a few days, you simply miss most of these waves. You can adopt the principle without an Enterprise license too, for example with Dependabot’s cooldown option.

News on the Claude API and Agent Skills

Claude API 2026-10-21 rejects temperature and top_p

Anthropic released API version 2026-10-21 on October 21. With it, requests containing temperature, top_p or top_k fail with an HTTP 400 error, even if the values match the defaults. At the same time, new major SDK versions came out that send the new version automatically, including TypeScript SDK 1.0.0, Python SDK 2.0.0 and Java SDK 3.0.0. They bring breaking changes of their own: the API key is now sent as Authorization: Bearer instead of X-Api-Key, and the license switches from MIT to Apache 2.0. On Amazon Bedrock, the new version only works with Claude 4.7 and newer.

My advice: do not let Dependabot auto-merge PRs for @anthropic-ai/sdk this time. First search your code for sampling parameters and check whether a gateway, proxy or log filter depends on the old header. You will find the individual steps with code examples in Claude API 2026-10-21: migrating to the new SDK.

Agent Skills move to the Agentic AI Foundation

On October 22, Anthropic handed Agent Skills over to the Agentic AI Foundation, a foundation within the Linux Foundation. Behind the term is a simple format: a SKILL.md in a folder, optionally with scripts, that gives an AI agent domain knowledge and workflows. Besides the specification, the name and logo, the project’s GitHub account and agentskills.io change hands as well. According to Anthropic, more than 70 agent platforms have adopted the standard since December 2025, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code. Going forward, people from several companies will maintain it, among them Anthropic, Google and OpenAI. Versioned releases, a formal process for change proposals and security guidelines are planned.

MCP took the same path before, and I think it is the right one. A standard that no single vendor owns makes it easier to invest time in good skills. I show how to write a SKILL.md that works across several agents in Writing Agent Skills.

Serverless, AWS and TypeScript

CloudFormation Force Rollback rescues stuck stacks

Since October 22, CloudFormation offers a force rollback option when you continue an update rollback. Until now, for a stack in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state you had to name and skip every stuck resource individually. Now CloudFormation does this in one step and returns the stack to a state you can deploy from again. Resources that still need attention are recorded. The feature is available in all Regions at no extra cost and also works with the AWS CDK, the CLI and the SDKs.

Anyone who has spent a night in front of a stuck stack will appreciate this. Still, force rollback is the emergency exit, not the normal case. Afterwards the stack no longer matches the template exactly, so before your next deploy a drift-aware change set that shows you the differences is worth it. The commands are in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED: rescue a stack with force rollback.

TypeScript 7.1 Beta type-checks up to 47 percent faster

Microsoft released the beta of TypeScript 7.1 on October 20, the first feature release since the switch to the native compiler in 7.0. In the TypeScript team’s benchmarks, type-checking time drops by 13 to 47 percent compared to 7.0, depending on the project, and memory usage by 16 to 50 percent. In addition, es2026 is now a stable value for --target and --lib, and the compiler API is split into several entry points such as typescript/sync and typescript/ast. The release candidate is expected about a month after the beta.

Trying it out costs you little: run npm install -D typescript@beta on a separate branch and let your CI run. Keep an eye on tools built on the compiler API, such as linter plugins or framework checkers. The most important changes and a test guide are in Testing TypeScript 7.1 Beta.

My takeaways from Serverless & AI in brief, week 43

This week shows nicely how closely the topics are intertwined by now. A problem at a certificate authority reaches browsers, Node.js, Java and AWS within a few days. Meanwhile, tools for AI agents are growing up: open standards, versioned APIs and real breaking changes come with the same duties we know from every other dependency.

If you only have half an hour, I would go in this order:

  1. Before October 28, check the certificate chains of CloudFront origins and of identity providers behind ALBs.
  2. Upgrade Node.js to 26.12.1, 24.22.1 or 22.23.4 everywhere, including containers and CI.
  3. Plan Claude SDK upgrades deliberately instead of merging them automatically.
  4. Introduce a waiting period for new npm versions, with the Package Firewall or with Dependabot.

What comes next in Serverless & AI in brief

The next review will appear on Monday, November 2, and covers week 44. I collect all issues on the page Series: Serverless & AI in brief. I would rather include four good items than seven thin ones. If you think an important piece of news is missing, feel free to add it in the comments.

Now over to you: which of these seven items actually created work for your team this week?

title: Multi-agent system for business: when to build a team
excerpt: If there are only a few tasks and scenarios, one general-purpose AI agent is enough. There's no need to create a complex architecture for that. When the work includes major areas, I give each agent
content:
If there are only a few tasks and scenarios, one general-purpose AI agent is enough. There's no need to create a complex architecture for that. When the work includes major areas, I give each agent a specific role

For me, the sign is a task that comes up regularly and needs its own knowledge base, memory, and tools. It's the same principle as hiring an employee: first, you need to know what work you'll give them

Where to start dividing the work

Take content production as an example. You regularly write posts and need images to go with them. Those are two areas: one handles the text, the other handles the visuals. You can assign a copywriter and a designer and define the result expected from each

The copywriter receives a topic and source material. Its job is to prepare the text. The designer receives the approved topic and the post's message, then creates an image based on them. Each agent has a clear assignment instead of just a job title on a list

What the copywriter needs

Telling an agent "write posts" isn't enough. It needs writing rules and examples of your style: how you address your reader, what expressions you use, and what should stay out of the text. Its writing skills and tools are set up for that work

When you edit a text, it's important for the agent to keep those lessons in memory. For example, if you remove a repeated idea, that can become a rule for the next post. This helps the copywriter gradually get closer to your style

How to connect the designer's work

The designer doesn't need the whole set of writing rules. It needs the message of the text and the image requirements: format, visual style, and what should appear in the frame. It has its own skills and tools for images and video

The handoff between agents matters too. If the designer starts with a draft and the text changes afterward, the image may no longer fit. That's why it's worth defining which version of the text goes to the designer and who checks the finished post and image together

Each agent is essentially a separate employee. You wouldn't expect your secretary to be an accountant, programmer, and designer all at once: they'd simply explode. The same applies to agents

An AI system architecture helps define these roles and connect them into a working process

Half joke. Planning poker made sense when a 5 point ticket meant a few days of someone's time. Now Claude Code or Cursor can draft that ticket before lunch, and the slow part moved to review and testing. Estimating the typing doesn't tell you much anymore.

  • Estimating review time instead of build time

title: Building a baby memory book with SwiftUI
excerpt:
A photo can show a baby's first smile. A caption can preserve what happened just before it.

That is the kind of detail I wanted Pagewren to make room for: a picture, a few words, and a page
content:
A photo can show a baby's first smile. A caption can preserve what happened just before it.

That is the kind of detail I wanted Pagewren to make room for: a picture, a few words, and a page someone might want to return to years later.

I'm the developer of Pagewren, a baby memory book for iPhone. The central design decision was to put the book itself on the home screen. Add a memory, and it becomes part of the book you're already reading.

That decision also shaped some interesting engineering work.

Making each entry feel finished

The capture flow accepts photos, words, or both. Pagewren arranges the content into a page, with chapters organized around the child's age.

For a keepsake app, that immediate result matters. If saving a memory also leaves you with a layout task, there is more work waiting the next time you open it. I wanted the output of a small entry to feel complete enough to keep.

There are no daily streaks. Parents can add an ordinary moment, leave a gap, and come back later. Batch photo import helps them bring older memories into the book too.

Sharing the page renderer

Pagewren is built with SwiftUI. Its book pages use a shared BookPageView that receives the page content, the selected style, and the rendering width.

The PDF exporter uses that same view through ImageRenderer, drawing it into a PDF graphics context. Page dimensions and typography scale from the page width.

This keeps layout decisions in one place. Changing how a theme places a photograph does not require a separate implementation of that layout for export.

The rendering context still needs a few differences. A printed page has square corners. Interactive controls belong in the app. But the composition comes from the same component.

One detail that matters here is image loading. Export does not wait for an asynchronous image request to finish. The page renderer therefore receives a synchronous image source, so the photos are available when the page is drawn.

It is a small interface choice with a visible consequence: a page exported with its pictures in place.

Measuring words before splitting pages

Pagination becomes more involved once a memory can include a short caption, a long story, or a list.

Pagewren measures text using TextKit and the font and available text area for the chosen layout. A photo page has less space for words than a text page. Different themes also leave different amounts of room.

The page break follows the laid-out lines. List items and embedded elements need their own handling so they do not get split arbitrarily across pages.

For this app, measuring the actual text is much more useful than treating a page as a fixed number of characters. The visible line breaks are what determine whether the words fit.

Keeping the book on the device

The persistence layer uses Core Data, with optional CloudKit mirroring for Pro users.

The app can open the local store without enabling sync. When CloudKit cannot be initialized, the persistence controller attempts to open the same store locally. That fallback keeps the storage path centered on the book already on the phone.

There is no Pagewren account to create. Book content stays on the iPhone and, when sync is enabled, in the user's private iCloud database. Usage analytics and crash reporting are separate from the photos and writing in the book.

For the public details, see the app's privacy information on the App Store.

Letting people take the book with them

PDF export is a useful part of the product: it gives the parent a file they can save or share. Individual pages can also be shared as images.

That requirement makes the shared renderer more than a code organization preference. Exported pages are part of the experience people keep outside the app.

Pagewren is available on the App Store. It is free to download and use with the Classic theme. Pro adds themes, iCloud sync, and Privacy Lock, with monthly, yearly, and lifetime purchase options.

I'd be interested to hear from other developers building journals or tools for personal archives: how do you keep the capture flow small while giving people something satisfying to come back to?

title: The Power of git rebase --onto: Surgical Commit Slicing in Git
excerpt:
If you work in a team that stacks branches or uses Squash & Merge, you have almost certainly encountered this nightmare:

  1. You create branch feature-B
content:
If you work in a team that stacks branches or uses Squash & Merge, you have almost certainly encountered this nightmare:

  1. You create branch feature-B off feature-A while waiting for review.
  2. feature-A gets approved and squash-merged into main.
  3. You open a Pull Request for feature-B against main.
  4. Disaster: Your PR suddenly includes all 20 commits from feature-A, hundreds of duplicate lines of diff, and a maze of merge conflicts.

A standard git rebase main often gets confused because the commit hashes of feature-A no longer exist on main (they were replaced by a single squash commit).

This is where Git's most underrated surgical tool comes in: git rebase --onto.

The Mental Model: Git as Scissors & Glue

A standard rebase says:

"Take everything on my branch since it diverged from main, and replay it on top of main."

The --onto flag gives you precision scissors:

"Take only the commits between point X and point Y, cut them out, and glue them onto point Z."

Syntax Breakdown 


bash
git rebase --onto <new-base> <old-base> [<branch>]

title: AWS Architecture Design: Secure, Resilient & Cost-Optimised
excerpt: Designing a new system on Amazon Web Services (AWS) includes planning and building scalable and secure infrastructure using core services. But the responsibility isn’t restricted to ensuring scalab
content:
Designing a new system on Amazon Web Services (AWS) includes planning and building scalable and secure infrastructure using core services. But the responsibility isn’t restricted to ensuring scalability. You must also ensure that the system is safe, runs efficiently, and doesn’t inflate the company budget. This is where the role of an AWS solutions architect becomes important.

This article is a breakdown for professionals to design a secure, resilient, high-performing, and cost-effective AWS solution. These design areas give you a clear framework to work from, especially when designing the system for the first time.

Why does an AWS Architecture Design Matters?

AWS design principles are basically the rules that govern your choices, especially since there are several ways to build a cloud solution.
Here are a few instances:

  • Maintain access control so any unauthorised user cannot make any changes.
  • Use multi-AZ deployments so that the application keeps running even if a component fails.
  • Planning scalability solutions so that the cloud system can handle the changing requirements.
  • Data encryption so the user's sensitive information is always safe.

Working on high-performance architectures helps design solutions that require minimal changes after launch. Redesigning a solution or working on an existing system requires extra time and effort. That’s why the AWS design matters.

AWS follows a Well-Architected Framework which covers the following core areas:

  • Operational excellence
  • Security
  • Reliability
  • performance efficiency
  • cost optimisation
  • Sustainability There are six pillars in the AWS Well-Architected Framework, however, the building of a solution is more about security, resilience, performance and cost optimisation.

What is Multi-Tier Architecture?


A multi-tier architecture breaks down an application into various layers, and each layer performs a specific task. It enables you to deploy application components, manage access and scale resources efficiently.

There are three levels:

Presentation tier

This layer receives incoming requests via an app/website. Elastic Load Balancing and Amazon CloudFront are also helpful for content delivery and traffic distribution.

Application tier

The second layer handles requests and application logic. AWS Lambda and EC2 can efficiently handle these workloads depending on the requirements of the current application.

Data tier

The last layer is in charge of storing and managing the data of the application. You can use Amazon RDS for relational databases and Amazon DynamoDB for a managed NoSQL database.

Architects commonly depend on Auto Scaling to adjust the compute capacity and meet the ongoing demand. They also divide resources across multiple Availability Zones.

However, every AWS solution would not go through the same process. It ultimately depends on the application’s complexity, security requirements, availability targets and budget.

Let’s look at the key design principles, relevant AWS services, and example architectures for each of these four areas.

Design Secure Solutions

Security is a critical part of AWS architecture design. Architects must ensure that users and services have only the permissions they need, protect sensitive information, and monitor activity to identify potential threats.

Key services of a secure AWS architecture:

  • AWS IAM controls everyone’s roles so there is no chance of password leaks.
  • Security groups work as virtual firewalls, only allowing the traffic that’s on the list.
  • AWS KMS creates keys for encryption in Amazon RDS, EBS and S3.
  • The managed web application firewall (WAF) blocks web attacks before they can interfere with the server.

Example:

AWS is hosting an eCommerce application that runs in a Virtual Private Cloud. In this app, only the load balancer faces the internet, while the web, app and database are present in the private subnets. This database is encrypted through a KMS key, and the traffic uses TLS. In case an attacker is able to find a loophole in the web, they still cannot access the database. That’s how the architecture works.

In case a reliable professional (architect) isn’t available on site, teams often make the mistake of opening the security group to the public for testing and forget to close it.

Ensure Resilient Architecture

If a design is fault-tolerant or covers the downtime quickly, your cloud will keep operating at all times. An architect’s job is to identify the possible failure points and plan for backup and recovery along with distributing workloads across multiple Availability Zones. The exact approach depends on the application requirements.

Key services of a resilient AWS architecture:

  • The Elastic Load Balancing checks the server health and sends traffic only to the working ones.
  • Auto Scaling can replace failed instances with the ones that are working.
  • AWS Backup helps in automated data protection across services.
  • Amazon SQS enables tiers to work independently so that a slow part does not freeze the rest.

Example:

Every app tier runs in two Availability Zones. In case one goes down or its server fails the health check, the load balancer stops sending users there. Meanwhile, the other zone continues to receive traffic. Auto Scaling launches new instances to replace failed ones and RDS promotes the standby database in Zone B, typically within one to two minutes. In such instances, there may be a slight delay for users.

Focus on High-Performing Architecture

A high-performing architecture matches the expectations when computing, storing, and using networking resources efficiently. An architect is majorly responsible for selecting a suitable resource type, identifying bottlenecks, and monitoring performance for every workload.
When working on cloud solutions, performance isn’t restricted to big servers. It shifts to picking the right resource for every job.

Key services include the following:

  • Amazon CloudFront that delivers content through a global content delivery network.
  • Amazon ElastiCache to maintain backup so there are minimal queries.
  • Amazon EC2 provides a customisable computing capacity for workloads.
  • Amazon CloudWatch collects logs so that the architect can monitor the application performance.

Example:

Let’s say a website is busy every evening. CloudFront will serve images from locations closest to every visitor. So most of the requests don’t reach your servers. At the same time, ElastiCache keeps the database consolidated. At times when the traffic grows, Lambda is beneficial for working in the background on tasks like resizing an uploaded photo.

Optimise Cost for Every Solution

When an architecture is cost-saving, it meets the business requirements without paying for extra resources. An architect is responsible for matching capacity with the workload demand and choosing a suitable pricing model accordingly. However, cost optimization should not come at the expense of the solution’s security or performance.

Key services of a cost-optimised architecture:

  • A savings plan saves cost over long-term usage.
  • Spot Instances utilises spare AWS capacity at a discount and can be interrupted. Always use them for work that’s dispensable.
  • S3 storage classes and lifecycle rules shift old data to better storage options automatically.
  • AWS Budgets and Cost Explorer keeps a track of the expenses and give warnings early.

Example:

Imagine that an application gets extensively used during business hours. However, the demand reduces at night. The Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the events according to the workload requirements. Your team can utilize Compute Optimiser for review and Cost Explorer to keep a track of spending. These measures help control costs and maintain the needed capacity.

The four designs closely relate to each other. An AWS architect has to evaluate the trade-offs to find the best solutions and meet the requirements simultaneously.

You can learn more about the AWS design principles from the official Microsoft documentation.

What are the Common Trade-Offs in AWS Architecture Design?

When you are designing an AWS architecture, you have to maintain a balance between the requirements. A choice can improve one area but compromise the other. That’s where an AWS architect comes into action and evaluates these tradeoffs.

Conclusion

An efficient architecture should balance security, resilience, performance and cost optimisation. It is important to understand how these areas interact to be able to make informed decisions and build solutions that meet business needs. Professionals may prepare for real-world cloud challenges by implementing these principles through hands-on labs and practice papers.

The AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate certification provides a pathway for professionals who want to validate these skills and prove their knowledge of how to design secure, resilient, high-performing and cost-optimised solutions on AWS.

title: Cloudflare vs Namecheap: Which .com Renewal Is Cheaper in 2026?
excerpt:
Cloudflare vs Namecheap: Which .com Renewal Is Cheaper in 2026?

Namecheap is where many of us bought our first domain. Cloudflare Registrar is where many of us move it. The reas
content:
Cloudflare vs Namecheap: Which .com Renewal Is Cheaper in 2026?

Namecheap is where many of us bought our first domain. Cloudflare Registrar is where many of us move it. The reason is simple: renewal price. Here is the honest comparison.

The renewal prices

Prices checked 28 October 2026:

  • Cloudflare Registrar — $10.44 total. At-cost pricing: Verisign wholesale $10.26 + $0.18 ICANN fee, with no markup at all.
  • Namecheap — $18.48 total. That is $8.04 more per year, every year, for the same .com.
  • Over five years, one domain costs about $52 at Cloudflare versus about $92 at Namecheap — a $40 difference for nothing extra.

The full price comparison lives here: https://renewpings.com/blog/cheapest-com-renewal-prices

What you actually get

Cloudflare sells domains at cost and includes free WHOIS privacy. The catch: you must use Cloudflare's nameservers, and the dashboard is built for people comfortable with DNS settings. It is not the friendliest first registrar.

Namecheap costs more, but the dashboard is easier, support answers faster, and moving a domain in or out is simple. For a beginner, that ease is worth something — just not $8 a year forever.

Which one should you pick?

  • You are comfortable with DNS: Cloudflare wins on price, every time.
  • You want the easiest dashboard and support: Namecheap is fine — just know you are paying a premium for it.
  • You have several domains: the saving multiplies. Ten domains save about $80 a year at Cloudflare.

One warning before you renew

Verisign's wholesale .com price rises from $10.26 to $10.97 on 1 November 2026, so at-cost renewals will creep up everywhere. If your domain expires soon, renewing before that date locks in the current rate. The full side-by-side is here: https://renewpings.com/blog/cloudflare-vs-namecheap-renewal-cost — and the whole comparison tool is at https://renewpings.com/compare

Bottom line: Cloudflare is the cheaper renewal by a clear margin. Namecheap is the easier experience. Pick the one that matches how hands-on you want to be.

content:

Review the details, PolyShell infection vectors, cloud exposure statistics from Wiz, and multi-vendor patch advisories including Node.js.

The problem in the Brotli library

The first issue concerns the Brotli data compression tool, which is widely used in a number of applications and services worldwide. This vulnerability, known as Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell or Broccoli2Shell, could allow an attacker to corrupt a system's memory, cause a system crash, or even execute code remotely if the application processes data sent by a malicious user.

Security firms have detected web traffic attempting to exploit this issue, with attempts recorded coming from IP addresses in the United States and the Netherlands, among others. Meanwhile, estimates from Wiz indicate that the vast majority of cloud computing environments have affected resources, with a significant percentage maintaining publicly exposed Node.js installations.

Due to the widespread use of Brotli, dozens of developers and software providers, including PHP, Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, .NET, Python, and others, have rushed to release security updates. For example, Node.js fixed the issue in versions 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1.

Attacks on online stores

The second issue is found in the Adobe Commerce and Magento platforms. This vulnerability concerns the ability to upload files without the necessary restrictions, allowing unknown parties to execute code and potentially gain control over user accounts or sessions.

title: Top WordPress MCP Server Plugins You Can Use in 2026
excerpt:
What if your AI could actually work on your WordPress site, not just talk about it?

Ask it to write a new post and save it as a draft. Update product descriptions in your store. Clean up ol
content:
What if your AI could actually work on your WordPress site, not just talk about it?

Ask it to write a new post and save it as a draft. Update product descriptions in your store. Clean up old comments. Add alt text to your images. Change your site settings without searching through wp-admin.

No copying. No pasting. No clicking through screen after screen. You ask, and your AI does it on your site.

That’s what a WordPress MCP server plugin makes possible. It connects your site to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another AI assistant, so the AI can handle a lot of what you’d usually do in wp-admin yourself, inside the limits you set.

Here are the top WordPress MCP server plugins in 2026, what each one lets your AI do, and how to choose the right one safely.

Key Takeaways

  • A WordPress MCP plugin lets AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor read and change your site through approved actions.

  • Some plugins connect your AI tool straight to your site. Others route requests through the vendor’s own service.

  • The official MCP Adapter is the foundation, and companion plugins make it easier to control.

  • Safety features vary a lot: drafts by default, read-only access, approvals, undo and activity logs.

  • Run one MCP plugin at a time, and test on a staging site first.

What is a WordPress MCP server plugin, and what does it do?

A WordPress MCP server plugin turns your site into an MCP server. AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can then read and update your content through a set of approved actions. Instead of telling you what to click, the AI does the work on your site, and you decide what it is allowed to touch.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to other software in a consistent way. When a WordPress site speaks MCP, any compatible AI tool can discover what the site allows, such as creating a draft post or updating an SEO title.

💡

Notes: WordPress itself now provides the building blocks. The Abilities API, part of WordPress core since version 6.9, lets plugins describe what they can do. If you want the technical background, our Abilities API and MCP guide covers how the pieces fit together.

Where is MCP already built in without a separate plugin?

Some WordPress platforms and popular plugins now include MCP support themselves, so you may not need a separate MCP plugin for every job. Three are worth knowing about, though two are still in early stages.

WordPress.com

WordPress.com includes MCP on all paid plans, so there is nothing to install. You turn it on under Preferences > AI and MCP. AI tools can then read your content, stats and settings, and create, edit or delete content when write access is on. See the WordPress.com MCP documentation for details.

WooCommerce

WooCommerce includes native MCP support built on the Abilities API and MCP Adapter, covering products and orders. It is still a developer preview, so most store owners will want to wait for a stable release. The WooCommerce MCP documentation tracks its progress.

Elementor

Elementor opened a beta of Elementor MCP in September 2026. It lets AI build and edit pages, manage the design system and create theme parts, and saves everything as drafts. Details are in the Elementor MCP beta announcement.

How can you see what AI is doing on your site once it’s connected?

Once a WordPress MCP server plugin lets AI change your site, you need a clear record of what the AI did, when, and on whose behalf. Several MCP plugins in this guide include their own logs, and a dedicated tracker gives you one place to review MCP activity in wp-admin.

Easy MCP AI, Royal MCP, Secure MCP Server and WPVibe each keep their own record of AI actions. If your setup is built on the Abilities API, MCP Tracker by WPVibes adds a separate, consistent view.

MCP Tracker logs MCP requests made to the Abilities API on your WordPress site. For every request, it records the route, the request details, the response, and which WordPress user made it. You can filter the log by date range, tool name and user, and open any entry to read the full request and response.

MCP Tracker only watches. It never changes or blocks a request, and every log stays in your own WordPress database with nothing sent outside your site. Only administrators can open the MCP Tracker screen.

How do you choose the right MCP server plugin for your site?

The right WordPress MCP server plugin depends on what your site does and who will use the AI connection. There is no single best choice, so start from your situation and look for the MCP plugins whose features match it.

  • You run a WooCommerce store: look at plugins with WooCommerce tools, such as Easy MCP AI, Royal MCP, Secure MCP Server, Enable Abilities for MCP, AcrossAI, and WPVibe. AI Engine adds WooCommerce tools in its Pro version.

  • You build with a page builder: check builder support first. Royal MCP and Secure MCP Server cover Elementor and Divi, WPVibe lists several builders including Bricks, AcrossAI, and Enable Abilities for MCP include Elementor abilities.

  • You manage client sites: look for role-based access and separate connections, like the Agent Registry in Secure MCP Server, the per-client servers in AcrossAI, or fleet updates in WPVibe.

  • You want everything on your own server: choose a plugin that connects directly, which is every plugin here except WPVibe.

  • You want the easiest start: one-click connect flows in Easy MCP AI, AcrossAI, and WPVibe get you running quickly.

  • You are a developer on staging: Novamira gives full access for building and debugging.

What should you check before installing a WordPress MCP server plugin?

Before you install a WordPress MCP server plugin, check where it runs, what it can change, and how you will review its work. A few habits make the difference between a helpful AI assistant and a stressful one.

  • Test on a staging site first, and keep a recent backup.
  • Start with read-only access, then add write access step by step.
  • Connect with a WordPress user whose role fits the job, not always an administrator.
  • Turn on drafts for anything the AI creates, so you review before it goes live.
  • Keep an activity log/debug log switched on.
  • Run one MCP plugin at a time.
  • Check whether requests go directly to your site or through a vendor’s service.

Thinking about how AI tools read your public content too? Our guide to making your site readable to AI tools with llms.txt covers the other side of the picture.

Ready to let AI work on your WordPress site with confidence?

WordPress MCP server plugins differ in three main ways: how they connect, what they let AI control, and how easily you can limit and review that work. Match those three to your site, test on staging, and grow access as trust builds.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an official WordPress MCP plugin?

Yes. MCP Adapter is the official plugin from WordPress.org, part of the AI Building Blocks for WordPress initiative. It connects the Abilities API to MCP so AI tools can use your site's abilities. It adds no AI features itself, so most site owners pair it with a companion plugin for easier control.

Can ChatGPT or Claude edit my WordPress site?

Yes, once you install an MCP plugin and approve the connection. ChatGPT and Claude can then create drafts, update content and handle other tasks the plugin allows. What they can change depends on the plugin's settings and the WordPress user role you connect with.

Is it safe to connect AI to my WordPress site?

It can be, if you set limits. Start on a staging site, use read-only access first, connect with a suitable user role, and keep an activity log on. Choose a plugin with safeguards such as drafts by default, approvals for destructive actions, or an undo option.

Do I need a plugin for MCP on WordPress.com?

No. WordPress.com includes MCP on all paid plans, so you turn it on under Preferences > AI and MCP instead of installing a plugin.

How do I see what an AI agent changed on my site?

Use the activity log in your MCP plugin, if it has one, or add a dedicated tracker. MCP Tracker by WPVibes logs MCP requests made to the Abilities API, showing the user, the tool and the full response, with filters by date, tool and user.

Whichever MCP plugin you choose, give every AI action a paper trail. Install MCP Tracker by WPVibes for free and see each MCP request, who made it, and what came back. Get MCP Tracker.
